# async-broadcast 0.7.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/async-broadcast/0.7.2

# async-broadcast

An async multi-producer multi-consumer broadcast channel, where each consumer gets a clone of every
message sent on the channel. For obvious reasons, the channel can only be used to broadcast types
that implement `Clone`.

A channel has the `Sender` and `Receiver` side. Both sides are cloneable and can be shared
among multiple threads.

When all `Sender`s or all `Receiver`s are dropped, the channel becomes closed. When a channel is
closed, no more messages can be sent, but remaining messages can still be received.

The channel can also be closed manually by calling `Sender::close()` or
`Receiver::close()`.

## Examples

```
use ;
use ;
block_on
```
## Difference with `async-channel`

This crate is similar to [ async-channel](https://crates.io/crates/async-channel) in that they both provide an MPMC channel but the main
difference being that in

`async-channel`, each message sent on the channel is only received by one
of the receivers. `async-broadcast` on the other hand, delivers each message to every receiver
(IOW broadcast) by cloning it for each receiver.## Difference with other broadcast crates

-
`broadcaster``broadcaster`doesn't have a sender and receiver split and both sides use clones of the same BroadcastChannel instance. The messages are sent are sent to all channel clones. While this can work for many cases, the lack of sender and receiver split, means that often times, you'll find yourself having to drain the channel on the sending side yourself.
-
`postage`[broadcast API](https://docs.rs/postage/0.4.1/postage/broadcast/fn.channel.html)similar to`async_broadcast`. However, it:- (at the time of this writing) duplicates [futures](https://crates.io/crates/futures)API, which isn't ideal.
- Does not support overflow mode nor has the concept of inactive receivers, so a slow or inactive receiver blocking the whole channel is not a solvable problem.
- Provides all kinds of channels, which is generally good but if you just need a broadcast
channel, `async_broadcast`is probably a better choice.

- (at the time of this writing) duplicates
-
`tokio::sync``sync`module provides a[broadcast channel](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.6.0/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html)API. The differences here are:- While this implementation does provide [overflow mode](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.6.0/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html#lagging), it is the default behavior and not opt-in.
- There is no equivalent of inactive receivers.
- While it's possible to build tokio with only the `sync`module, it comes with other APIs that you may not need.

- While this implementation does provide

## Safety

This crate uses `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` to ensure everything is implemented in
100% Safe Rust.

## Contributing

look at some of these issues:

# async_broadcast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/async-broadcast/0.7.2/target-redirect/async_broadcast/

## Expand description

Async broadcast channel

An async multi-producer multi-consumer broadcast channel, where each consumer gets a clone of every
message sent on the channel. For obvious reasons, the channel can only be used to broadcast types
that implement [ Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html).

A channel has the [ Sender](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html) and

[side. Both sides are cloneable and can be shared among multiple threads.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)

`Receiver`When all `Sender`s or all `Receiver`s are dropped, the channel becomes closed. When a channel is
closed, no more messages can be sent, but remaining messages can still be received.

The channel can also be closed manually by calling [ Sender::close()](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.close) or

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.close)

`Receiver::close()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TryRecvError};
use futures_lite::{future::block_on, stream::StreamExt};
block_on(async move {
    let (s1, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
    let s2 = s1.clone();
    let mut r2 = r1.clone();
    // Send 2 messages from two different senders.
    s1.broadcast(7).await.unwrap();
    s2.broadcast(8).await.unwrap();
    // Channel is now at capacity so sending more messages will result in an error.
    assert!(s2.try_broadcast(9).unwrap_err().is_full());
    assert!(s1.try_broadcast(10).unwrap_err().is_full());
    // We can use `recv` method of the `Stream` implementation to receive messages.
    assert_eq!(r1.next().await.unwrap(), 7);
    assert_eq!(r1.recv().await.unwrap(), 8);
    assert_eq!(r2.next().await.unwrap(), 7);
    assert_eq!(r2.recv().await.unwrap(), 8);
    // All receiver got all messages so channel is now empty.
    assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
    assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
    // Drop both senders, which closes the channel.
    drop(s1);
    drop(s2);
    assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
    assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
})
```
[§](https://docs.rs#difference-with-async-channel)Difference with `async-channel`

This crate is similar to [ async-channel](https://crates.io/crates/async-channel) in that they both provide an MPMC channel but the
main difference being that in

`async-channel`, each message sent on the channel is only received
by one of the receivers. `async-broadcast` on the other hand, delivers each message to every
receiver (IOW broadcast) by cloning it for each receiver.[§](https://docs.rs#difference-with-other-broadcast-crates)Difference with other broadcast crates

-
`broadcaster``broadcaster`doesn’t have a sender and receiver split and both sides use clones of the same BroadcastChannel instance. The messages are sent are sent to all channel clones. While this can work for many cases, the lack of sender and receiver split, means that often times, you’ll find yourself having to drain the channel on the sending side yourself.
-
`postage`[broadcast API](https://docs.rs/postage/0.4.1/postage/broadcast/fn.channel.html)similar to`async_broadcast`. However, it:- (at the time of this writing) duplicates [futures](https://crates.io/crates/futures)API, which isn’t ideal.
- Does not support overflow mode nor has the concept of inactive receivers, so a slow or inactive receiver blocking the whole channel is not a solvable problem.
- Provides all kinds of channels, which is generally good but if you just need a broadcast
channel, `async_broadcast`is probably a better choice.

- (at the time of this writing) duplicates
-
`tokio::sync``sync`module provides a[broadcast channel](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.6.0/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html)API. The differences here are:- While this implementation does provide [overflow mode](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.6.0/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html#lagging), it is the default behavior and not opt-in.
- There is no equivalent of inactive receivers.
- While it’s possible to build tokio with only the `sync`module, it comes with other APIs that you may not need.

- While this implementation does provide

# async_broadcast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/async-broadcast/0.7.2/async_broadcast/index.html

## Expand description

Async broadcast channel

An async multi-producer multi-consumer broadcast channel, where each consumer gets a clone of every
message sent on the channel. For obvious reasons, the channel can only be used to broadcast types
that implement [ Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html).

A channel has the [ Sender](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html) and

[side. Both sides are cloneable and can be shared among multiple threads.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)

`Receiver`When all `Sender`s or all `Receiver`s are dropped, the channel becomes closed. When a channel is
closed, no more messages can be sent, but remaining messages can still be received.

The channel can also be closed manually by calling [ Sender::close()](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.close) or

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.close)

`Receiver::close()`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TryRecvError};
use futures_lite::{future::block_on, stream::StreamExt};
block_on(async move {
    let (s1, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
    let s2 = s1.clone();
    let mut r2 = r1.clone();
    // Send 2 messages from two different senders.
    s1.broadcast(7).await.unwrap();
    s2.broadcast(8).await.unwrap();
    // Channel is now at capacity so sending more messages will result in an error.
    assert!(s2.try_broadcast(9).unwrap_err().is_full());
    assert!(s1.try_broadcast(10).unwrap_err().is_full());
    // We can use `recv` method of the `Stream` implementation to receive messages.
    assert_eq!(r1.next().await.unwrap(), 7);
    assert_eq!(r1.recv().await.unwrap(), 8);
    assert_eq!(r2.next().await.unwrap(), 7);
    assert_eq!(r2.recv().await.unwrap(), 8);
    // All receiver got all messages so channel is now empty.
    assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
    assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
    // Drop both senders, which closes the channel.
    drop(s1);
    drop(s2);
    assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
    assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
})
```
[§](https://docs.rs#difference-with-async-channel)Difference with `async-channel`

This crate is similar to [ async-channel](https://crates.io/crates/async-channel) in that they both provide an MPMC channel but the
main difference being that in

`async-channel`, each message sent on the channel is only received
by one of the receivers. `async-broadcast` on the other hand, delivers each message to every
receiver (IOW broadcast) by cloning it for each receiver.[§](https://docs.rs#difference-with-other-broadcast-crates)Difference with other broadcast crates

-
`broadcaster``broadcaster`doesn’t have a sender and receiver split and both sides use clones of the same BroadcastChannel instance. The messages are sent are sent to all channel clones. While this can work for many cases, the lack of sender and receiver split, means that often times, you’ll find yourself having to drain the channel on the sending side yourself.
-
`postage`[broadcast API](https://docs.rs/postage/0.4.1/postage/broadcast/fn.channel.html)similar to`async_broadcast`. However, it:- (at the time of this writing) duplicates [futures](https://crates.io/crates/futures)API, which isn’t ideal.
- Does not support overflow mode nor has the concept of inactive receivers, so a slow or inactive receiver blocking the whole channel is not a solvable problem.
- Provides all kinds of channels, which is generally good but if you just need a broadcast
channel, `async_broadcast`is probably a better choice.

- (at the time of this writing) duplicates
-
`tokio::sync``sync`module provides a[broadcast channel](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.6.0/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html)API. The differences here are:- While this implementation does provide [overflow mode](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.6.0/tokio/sync/broadcast/index.html#lagging), it is the default behavior and not opt-in.
- There is no equivalent of inactive receivers.
- While it’s possible to build tokio with only the `sync`module, it comes with other APIs that you may not need.

- While this implementation does provide

# async_broadcast/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Async broadcast channel
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! An async multi-producer multi-consumer broadcast channel, where each consumer gets a clone of every
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! message sent on the channel. For obvious reasons, the channel can only be used to broadcast types
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! that implement [`Clone`].
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//!
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! A channel has the [`Sender`] and [`Receiver`] side. Both sides are cloneable and can be shared
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! among multiple threads.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! When all `Sender`s or all `Receiver`s are dropped, the channel becomes closed. When a channel is
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! closed, no more messages can be sent, but remaining messages can still be received.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! The channel can also be closed manually by calling [`Sender::close()`] or [`Receiver::close()`].
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! ## Examples
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! ```rust
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TryRecvError};
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! use futures_lite::{future::block_on, stream::StreamExt};
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! block_on(async move {
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!     let (s1, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!     let s2 = s1.clone();
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!     let mut r2 = r1.clone();
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!     // Send 2 messages from two different senders.
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!     s1.broadcast(7).await.unwrap();
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!     s2.broadcast(8).await.unwrap();
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!     // Channel is now at capacity so sending more messages will result in an error.
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!     assert!(s2.try_broadcast(9).unwrap_err().is_full());
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!     assert!(s1.try_broadcast(10).unwrap_err().is_full());
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!     // We can use `recv` method of the `Stream` implementation to receive messages.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!     assert_eq!(r1.next().await.unwrap(), 7);
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!     assert_eq!(r1.recv().await.unwrap(), 8);
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!     assert_eq!(r2.next().await.unwrap(), 7);
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!     assert_eq!(r2.recv().await.unwrap(), 8);
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!     // All receiver got all messages so channel is now empty.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!     assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!     assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!

[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! })
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! ```

[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! ## Difference with `async-channel`
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! This crate is similar to [`async-channel`] in that they both provide an MPMC channel but the
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! main difference being that in `async-channel`, each message sent on the channel is only received
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! by one of the receivers. `async-broadcast` on the other hand, delivers each message to every
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! receiver (IOW broadcast) by cloning it for each receiver.
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! [`async-channel`]: https://crates.io/crates/async-channel
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! ## Difference with other broadcast crates
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! * [`broadcaster`]: The main difference would be that `broadcaster` doesn't have a sender and
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!   receiver split and both sides use clones of the same BroadcastChannel instance. The messages
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!   are sent are sent to all channel clones. While this can work for many cases, the lack of
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!   sender and receiver split, means that often times, you'll find yourself having to drain the
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!   channel on the sending side yourself.
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! * [`postage`]: this crate provides a [broadcast API][pba] similar to `async_broadcast`. However,
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!   it:
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!   - (at the time of this writing) duplicates [futures] API, which isn't ideal.
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!   - Does not support overflow mode nor has the concept of inactive receivers, so a slow or
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!     inactive receiver blocking the whole channel is not a solvable problem.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!   - Provides all kinds of channels, which is generally good but if you just need a broadcast
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!     channel, `async_broadcast` is probably a better choice.
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! * [`tokio::sync`]: Tokio's `sync` module provides a [broadcast channel][tbc] API. The differences
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!    here are:
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//!   - While this implementation does provide [overflow mode][tom], it is the default behavior and not
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!     opt-in.
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!   - There is no equivalent of inactive receivers.
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!   - While it's possible to build tokio with only the `sync` module, it comes with other APIs that
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!     you may not need.
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! [`broadcaster`]: https://crates.io/crates/broadcaster
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! [`postage`]: https://crates.io/crates/postage

[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! [futures]: https://crates.io/crates/futures

[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// Create a new broadcast channel.
[125](https://docs.rs#125)///
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// The created channel has space to hold at most `cap` messages at a time.
[127](https://docs.rs#127)///
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// # Panics
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// Capacity must be a positive number. If `cap` is zero, this function will panic.
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// # Examples
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///
[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// ```
[135](https://docs.rs#135)/// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TryRecvError, TrySendError};
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// let mut r2 = r1.clone();
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(10).await, Ok(None));
[142](https://docs.rs#142)/// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(20), Err(TrySendError::Full(20)));
[143](https://docs.rs#143)///
[144](https://docs.rs#144)/// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(10));
[145](https://docs.rs#145)/// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(10));
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[147](https://docs.rs#147)/// assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[148](https://docs.rs#148)/// # });
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// ```
[150](https://docs.rs#150)pub fn broadcast<T>(cap: usize) -> (Sender<T>, Receiver<T>) {
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    assert!(cap > 0, "capacity cannot be zero");
[152](https://docs.rs#152)
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    let inner = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Inner {
[154](https://docs.rs#154)        queue: VecDeque::with_capacity(cap),
[155](https://docs.rs#155)        capacity: cap,
[156](https://docs.rs#156)        overflow: false,
[157](https://docs.rs#157)        await_active: true,
[158](https://docs.rs#158)        receiver_count: 1,
[159](https://docs.rs#159)        inactive_receiver_count: 0,
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        sender_count: 1,
[161](https://docs.rs#161)        head_pos: 0,
[162](https://docs.rs#162)        is_closed: false,
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        send_ops: Event::new(),
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        recv_ops: Event::new(),
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    }));
[166](https://docs.rs#166)
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    let s = Sender {
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        inner: inner.clone(),
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    };
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    let r = Receiver {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)        inner,
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        pos: 0,
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        listener: None,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    };
[175](https://docs.rs#175)
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    (s, r)
[177](https://docs.rs#177)}
[178](https://docs.rs#178)
[179](https://docs.rs#179)#[derive(Debug)]
[180](https://docs.rs#180)struct Inner<T> {
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    queue: VecDeque<(T, usize)>,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    // We assign the same capacity to the queue but that's just specifying the minimum capacity and
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    // the actual capacity could be anything. Hence the need to keep track of our own set capacity.
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    capacity: usize,
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    receiver_count: usize,
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    inactive_receiver_count: usize,
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    sender_count: usize,
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    /// Send sequence number of the front of the queue
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    head_pos: u64,
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    overflow: bool,
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    await_active: bool,
[192](https://docs.rs#192)
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    is_closed: bool,
[194](https://docs.rs#194)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// Send operations waiting while the channel is full.
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    send_ops: Event,
[197](https://docs.rs#197)
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// Receive operations waiting while the channel is empty and not closed.
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    recv_ops: Event,
[200](https://docs.rs#200)}
[201](https://docs.rs#201)
[202](https://docs.rs#202)impl<T> Inner<T> {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// Try receiving at the given position, returning either the element or a reference to it.
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    ///
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// Result is used here instead of Cow because we don't have a Clone bound on T.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    fn try_recv_at(&mut self, pos: &mut u64) -> Result<Result<T, &T>, TryRecvError> {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        let i = match pos.checked_sub(self.head_pos) {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)            Some(i) => i
[209](https://docs.rs#209)                .try_into()
[210](https://docs.rs#210)                .expect("Head position more than usize::MAX behind a receiver"),
[211](https://docs.rs#211)            None => {
[212](https://docs.rs#212)                let count = self.head_pos - *pos;
[213](https://docs.rs#213)                *pos = self.head_pos;
[214](https://docs.rs#214)                return Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(count));
[215](https://docs.rs#215)            }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)        };
[217](https://docs.rs#217)
[218](https://docs.rs#218)        let last_waiter;
[219](https://docs.rs#219)        if let Some((_elt, waiters)) = self.queue.get_mut(i) {
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            *pos += 1;
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            *waiters -= 1;
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            last_waiter = *waiters == 0;
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        } else {
[224](https://docs.rs#224)            debug_assert_eq!(i, self.queue.len());
[225](https://docs.rs#225)            if self.is_closed {
[226](https://docs.rs#226)                return Err(TryRecvError::Closed);
[227](https://docs.rs#227)            } else {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                return Err(TryRecvError::Empty);
[229](https://docs.rs#229)            }
[230](https://docs.rs#230)        }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        // If we read from the front of the queue and this is the last receiver reading it
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        // we can pop the queue instead of cloning the message
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        if last_waiter {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            // Only the first element of the queue should have 0 waiters
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            assert_eq!(i, 0);
[237](https://docs.rs#237)
[238](https://docs.rs#238)            // Remove the element from the queue, adjust space, and notify senders
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            let elt = self.queue.pop_front().unwrap().0;
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            self.head_pos += 1;
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            if !self.overflow {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)                // Notify 1 awaiting senders that there is now room. If there is still room in the
[243](https://docs.rs#243)                // queue, the notified operation will notify another awaiting sender.
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                self.send_ops.notify(1);
[245](https://docs.rs#245)            }
[246](https://docs.rs#246)
[247](https://docs.rs#247)            Ok(Ok(elt))
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        } else {
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            Ok(Err(&self.queue[i].0))
[250](https://docs.rs#250)        }
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    }
[252](https://docs.rs#252)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// Closes the channel and notifies all waiting operations.
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    ///
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// Returns `true` if this call has closed the channel and it was not closed already.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    fn close(&mut self) -> bool {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)        if self.is_closed {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)            return false;
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        }
[260](https://docs.rs#260)
[261](https://docs.rs#261)        self.is_closed = true;
[262](https://docs.rs#262)        // Notify all waiting senders and receivers.
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        self.send_ops.notify(usize::MAX);
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        self.recv_ops.notify(usize::MAX);
[265](https://docs.rs#265)
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        true
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// Set the channel capacity.
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    ///
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// There are times when you need to change the channel's capacity after creating it. If the
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// `new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    /// dropped to shrink the channel.
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    fn set_capacity(&mut self, new_cap: usize) {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)        self.capacity = new_cap;
[276](https://docs.rs#276)        if new_cap > self.queue.capacity() {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)            let diff = new_cap - self.queue.capacity();
[278](https://docs.rs#278)            self.queue.reserve(diff);
[279](https://docs.rs#279)        }
[280](https://docs.rs#280)
[281](https://docs.rs#281)        // Ensure queue doesn't have more than `new_cap` messages.
[282](https://docs.rs#282)        if new_cap < self.queue.len() {
[283](https://docs.rs#283)            let diff = self.queue.len() - new_cap;
[284](https://docs.rs#284)            self.queue.drain(0..diff);
[285](https://docs.rs#285)            self.head_pos += diff as u64;
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    }
[288](https://docs.rs#288)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    /// Close the channel if there aren't any receivers present anymore
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    fn close_channel(&mut self) {
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        if self.receiver_count == 0 && self.inactive_receiver_count == 0 {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            self.close();
[293](https://docs.rs#293)        }
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    }
[295](https://docs.rs#295)}
[296](https://docs.rs#296)
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// The sending side of the broadcast channel.
[298](https://docs.rs#298)///
[299](https://docs.rs#299)/// Senders can be cloned and shared among threads. When all senders associated with a channel are
[300](https://docs.rs#300)/// dropped, the channel becomes closed.
[301](https://docs.rs#301)///
[302](https://docs.rs#302)/// The channel can also be closed manually by calling [`Sender::close()`].
[303](https://docs.rs#303)#[derive(Debug)]
[304](https://docs.rs#304)pub struct Sender<T> {
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner<T>>>,
[306](https://docs.rs#306)}
[307](https://docs.rs#307)
[308](https://docs.rs#308)impl<T> Sender<T> {
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    /// Returns the channel capacity.
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    ///
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    /// # Examples
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    ///
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    /// ```
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    ///
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    /// assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 5);
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    /// ```
[319](https://docs.rs#319)    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().capacity
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    }
[322](https://docs.rs#322)
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    /// Set the channel capacity.
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    ///
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// There are times when you need to change the channel's capacity after creating it. If the
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// `new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// dropped to shrink the channel.
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    ///
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    /// # Examples
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    ///
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    /// ```
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    ///
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    /// let (mut s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(3);
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    /// assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 3);
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    /// s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    /// s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    /// s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap();
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    ///
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    /// s.set_capacity(1);
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    /// assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 1);
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
[344](https://docs.rs#344)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    /// s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    ///
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    /// s.set_capacity(2);
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    /// assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 2);
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    /// s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// ```
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    pub fn set_capacity(&mut self, new_cap: usize) {
[354](https://docs.rs#354)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().set_capacity(new_cap);
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    /// If overflow mode is enabled on this channel.
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    ///
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    /// # Examples
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    ///
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    /// ```
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    ///
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    /// assert!(!s.overflow());
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    /// ```
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    pub fn overflow(&self) -> bool {
[368](https://docs.rs#368)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().overflow
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    }
[370](https://docs.rs#370)
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    /// Set overflow mode on the channel.
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    ///
[373](https://docs.rs#373)    /// When overflow mode is set, broadcasting to the channel will succeed even if the channel is
[374](https://docs.rs#374)    /// full. It achieves that by removing the oldest message from the channel.
[375](https://docs.rs#375)    ///
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// # Examples
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    ///
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    /// ```
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    ///
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    /// let (mut s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    /// s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    /// s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3), Err(TrySendError::Full(3)));
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    /// s.set_overflow(true);
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap(), Some(1));
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(4).unwrap(), Some(2));
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    ///
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 4);
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    /// ```
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    pub fn set_overflow(&mut self, overflow: bool) {
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().overflow = overflow;
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    }
[397](https://docs.rs#397)
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// If sender will wait for active receivers.
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    ///
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// If set to `false`, [`Send`] will resolve immediately with a [`SendError`]. Defaults to
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// `true`.
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    ///
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// # Examples
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    ///
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    /// ```
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    ///
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// let (s, _) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// assert!(s.await_active());
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    /// ```
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    pub fn await_active(&self) -> bool {
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().await_active
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    }
[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    /// Specify if sender will wait for active receivers.
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    ///
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    /// If set to `false`, [`Send`] will resolve immediately with a [`SendError`]. Defaults to
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    /// `true`.
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    ///
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    /// # Examples
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    ///
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    /// ```
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    ///
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// let (mut s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    ///
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// let _ = r.deactivate();
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// s.set_await_active(false);
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    /// assert!(s.broadcast(2).await.is_err());
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    /// # });
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// ```
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    pub fn set_await_active(&mut self, await_active: bool) {
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().await_active = await_active;
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    }
[437](https://docs.rs#437)
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    /// Closes the channel.
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    ///
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// Returns `true` if this call has closed the channel and it was not closed already.
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    ///
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    /// The remaining messages can still be received.
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    ///
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    /// # Examples
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    ///
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    /// ```
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[449](https://docs.rs#449)    ///
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    /// let (s, mut r) = broadcast(1);
[451](https://docs.rs#451)    /// s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
[452](https://docs.rs#452)    /// assert!(s.close());
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    ///
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await.unwrap(), 1);
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    /// # });
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    /// ```
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    pub fn close(&self) -> bool {
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().close()
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    }
[461](https://docs.rs#461)
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is closed.
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    ///
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    /// # Examples
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    ///
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    /// ```
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    ///
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<()>(1);
[471](https://docs.rs#471)    /// assert!(!s.is_closed());
[472](https://docs.rs#472)    ///
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    /// drop(r);
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    /// assert!(s.is_closed());
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    /// # });
[476](https://docs.rs#476)    /// ```
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
[478](https://docs.rs#478)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().is_closed
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    }
[480](https://docs.rs#480)
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is empty.
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    ///
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    /// # Examples
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    ///
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    /// ```
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    ///
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    ///
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    /// assert!(s.is_empty());
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    /// s.broadcast(1).await;
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    /// assert!(!s.is_empty());
[494](https://docs.rs#494)    /// # });
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    /// ```
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
[497](https://docs.rs#497)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().queue.is_empty()
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    }
[499](https://docs.rs#499)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is full.
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    ///
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    /// # Examples
[503](https://docs.rs#503)    ///
[504](https://docs.rs#504)    /// ```
[505](https://docs.rs#505)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    ///
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    ///
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    /// assert!(!s.is_full());
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    /// s.broadcast(1).await;
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    /// assert!(s.is_full());
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    /// # });
[514](https://docs.rs#514)    /// ```
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool {
[516](https://docs.rs#516)        let inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[517](https://docs.rs#517)
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        inner.queue.len() == inner.capacity
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    }
[520](https://docs.rs#520)
[521](https://docs.rs#521)    /// Returns the number of messages in the channel.
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    ///
[523](https://docs.rs#523)    /// # Examples
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    ///
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    /// ```
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    ///
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(2);
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// assert_eq!(s.len(), 0);
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    ///
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// s.broadcast(1).await;
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    /// s.broadcast(2).await;
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    /// assert_eq!(s.len(), 2);
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    /// # });
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    /// ```
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().queue.len()
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    }
[540](https://docs.rs#540)
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// Returns the number of receivers for the channel.
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    ///
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    /// This does not include inactive receivers. Use [`Sender::inactive_receiver_count`] if you
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    /// are interested in that.
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    ///
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    /// # Examples
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    ///
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    /// ```
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    ///
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<()>(1);
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    /// assert_eq!(s.receiver_count(), 1);
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    /// let r = r.deactivate();
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    /// assert_eq!(s.receiver_count(), 0);
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    ///
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    /// let r2 = r.activate_cloned();
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    /// assert_eq!(r.receiver_count(), 1);
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    /// assert_eq!(r.inactive_receiver_count(), 1);
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// ```
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    pub fn receiver_count(&self) -> usize {
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().receiver_count
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// Returns the number of inactive receivers for the channel.
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    ///
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    /// # Examples
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    ///
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// ```
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    ///
[571](https://docs.rs#571)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<()>(1);
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    /// assert_eq!(s.receiver_count(), 1);
[573](https://docs.rs#573)    /// let r = r.deactivate();
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    /// assert_eq!(s.receiver_count(), 0);
[575](https://docs.rs#575)    ///
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    /// let r2 = r.activate_cloned();
[577](https://docs.rs#577)    /// assert_eq!(r.receiver_count(), 1);
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    /// assert_eq!(r.inactive_receiver_count(), 1);
[579](https://docs.rs#579)    /// ```
[580](https://docs.rs#580)    pub fn inactive_receiver_count(&self) -> usize {
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().inactive_receiver_count
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    }
[583](https://docs.rs#583)
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Returns the number of senders for the channel.
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    ///
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// # Examples
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    ///
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    /// ```
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    ///
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<()>(1);
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    /// assert_eq!(s.sender_count(), 1);
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    ///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    /// let s2 = s.clone();
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    /// assert_eq!(s.sender_count(), 2);
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    /// # });
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    /// ```
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    pub fn sender_count(&self) -> usize {
[600](https://docs.rs#600)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().sender_count
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    }
[602](https://docs.rs#602)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// Produce a new Receiver for this channel.
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// The new receiver starts with zero messages available.  This will not re-open the channel if
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// it was closed due to all receivers being dropped.
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    ///
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    /// # Examples
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    ///
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// ```
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    ///
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    ///
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    ///
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    /// let mut r2 = s.new_receiver();
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    ///
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(2).await, Ok(None));
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    /// drop(s);
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    ///
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(2));
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    ///
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(2));
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    /// # });
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    /// ```
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    pub fn new_receiver(&self) -> Receiver<T> {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        inner.receiver_count += 1;
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        Receiver {
[635](https://docs.rs#635)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[636](https://docs.rs#636)            pos: inner.head_pos + inner.queue.len() as u64,
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            listener: None,
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    }
[640](https://docs.rs#640)}
[641](https://docs.rs#641)
[642](https://docs.rs#642)impl<T: Clone> Sender<T> {
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// Broadcasts a message on the channel.
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    ///
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// If the channel is full, this method waits until there is space for a message unless:
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    ///
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// 1. overflow mode (set through [`Sender::set_overflow`]) is enabled, in which case it removes
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    ///    the oldest message from the channel to make room for the new message. The removed message
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    ///    is returned to the caller.
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    /// 2. this behavior is disabled using [`Sender::set_await_active`], in which case, it returns
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    ///    [`SendError`] immediately.
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    ///
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    /// If the channel is closed, this method returns an error.
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    ///
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// The future returned by this function is pinned to the heap. If the future being `Unpin` is
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    /// not important to you, or if you just `.await` this future, use the [`broadcast_direct`] method
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    /// instead.
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    ///
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// # Examples
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// ```
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, SendError};
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    ///
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    ///
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    /// drop(r);
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(2).await, Err(SendError(2)));
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// # });
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    /// ```
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    pub fn broadcast(&self, msg: T) -> Pin<Box<Send<'_, T>>> {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        Box::pin(self.broadcast_direct(msg))
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    }
[675](https://docs.rs#675)
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// Broadcasts a message on the channel without pinning the future to the heap.
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    ///
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    /// The future returned by this method is not `Unpin` and must be pinned before use. This is
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    /// the desired behavior if you just `.await` on the future. For other uses cases, use the
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    /// [`broadcast`] method instead.
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    ///
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    /// # Examples
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    ///
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    /// ```
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, SendError};
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    ///
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    ///
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast_direct(1).await, Ok(None));
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    /// drop(r);
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast_direct(2).await, Err(SendError(2)));
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    /// # });
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// ```
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    pub fn broadcast_direct(&self, msg: T) -> Send<'_, T> {
[696](https://docs.rs#696)        Send::_new(SendInner {
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            sender: self,
[698](https://docs.rs#698)            listener: None,
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            msg: Some(msg),
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            _pin: PhantomPinned,
[701](https://docs.rs#701)        })
[702](https://docs.rs#702)    }
[703](https://docs.rs#703)
[704](https://docs.rs#704)    /// Attempts to broadcast a message on the channel.
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    ///
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    /// If the channel is full, this method returns an error unless overflow mode (set through
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// [`Sender::set_overflow`]) is enabled. If the overflow mode is enabled, it removes the
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// oldest message from the channel to make room for the new message. The removed message
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    /// is returned to the caller.
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    ///
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// If the channel is closed, this method returns an error.
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    ///
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// # Examples
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    ///
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    /// ```
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError};
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    ///
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    ///
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(1), Ok(None));
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    ///
[723](https://docs.rs#723)    /// drop(r);
[724](https://docs.rs#724)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3), Err(TrySendError::Closed(3)));
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    /// ```
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    pub fn try_broadcast(&self, msg: T) -> Result<Option<T>, TrySendError<T>> {
[727](https://docs.rs#727)        let mut ret = None;
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[729](https://docs.rs#729)
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        if inner.is_closed {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)            return Err(TrySendError::Closed(msg));
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        } else if inner.receiver_count == 0 {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)            assert!(inner.inactive_receiver_count != 0);
[734](https://docs.rs#734)
[735](https://docs.rs#735)            return Err(TrySendError::Inactive(msg));
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        } else if inner.queue.len() == inner.capacity {
[737](https://docs.rs#737)            if inner.overflow {
[738](https://docs.rs#738)                // Make room by popping a message.
[739](https://docs.rs#739)                ret = inner.queue.pop_front().map(|(m, _)| m);
[740](https://docs.rs#740)            } else {
[741](https://docs.rs#741)                return Err(TrySendError::Full(msg));
[742](https://docs.rs#742)            }
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        }
[744](https://docs.rs#744)        let receiver_count = inner.receiver_count;
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        inner.queue.push_back((msg, receiver_count));
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        if ret.is_some() {
[747](https://docs.rs#747)            inner.head_pos += 1;
[748](https://docs.rs#748)        }
[749](https://docs.rs#749)
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        // Notify all awaiting receive operations.
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        inner.recv_ops.notify(usize::MAX);
[752](https://docs.rs#752)
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        Ok(ret)
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    }
[755](https://docs.rs#755)
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    /// Broadcasts a message on the channel using the blocking strategy.
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    ///
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// If the channel is full, this method will block until there is room.
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    ///
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// If the channel is closed, this method returns an error.
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    ///
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    /// # Blocking
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    ///
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    /// Rather than using asynchronous waiting, like the [`send`](Self::broadcast) method,
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// this method will block the current thread until the message is sent.
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    ///
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    /// This method should not be used in an asynchronous context. It is intended
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    /// to be used such that a channel can be used in both asynchronous and synchronous contexts.
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    /// Calling this method in an asynchronous context may result in deadlocks.
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    ///
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    /// # Examples
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    ///
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    /// ```
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, SendError};
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    ///
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    ///
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast_blocking(1), Ok(None));
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    /// drop(r);
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast_blocking(2), Err(SendError(2)));
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    /// ```
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    #[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    pub fn broadcast_blocking(&self, msg: T) -> Result<Option<T>, SendError<T>> {
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        self.broadcast_direct(msg).wait()
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    }
[786](https://docs.rs#786)}
[787](https://docs.rs#787)
[788](https://docs.rs#788)impl<T> Drop for Sender<T> {
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[790](https://docs.rs#790)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[791](https://docs.rs#791)
[792](https://docs.rs#792)        inner.sender_count -= 1;
[793](https://docs.rs#793)
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        if inner.sender_count == 0 {
[795](https://docs.rs#795)            inner.close();
[796](https://docs.rs#796)        }
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    }
[798](https://docs.rs#798)}
[799](https://docs.rs#799)
[800](https://docs.rs#800)impl<T> Clone for Sender<T> {
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
[802](https://docs.rs#802)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().sender_count += 1;
[803](https://docs.rs#803)
[804](https://docs.rs#804)        Sender {
[805](https://docs.rs#805)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[806](https://docs.rs#806)        }
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    }
[808](https://docs.rs#808)}
[809](https://docs.rs#809)
[810](https://docs.rs#810)/// The receiving side of a channel.
[811](https://docs.rs#811)///
[812](https://docs.rs#812)/// Receivers can be cloned and shared among threads. When all (active) receivers associated with a
[813](https://docs.rs#813)/// channel are dropped, the channel becomes closed. You can deactivate a receiver using
[814](https://docs.rs#814)/// [`Receiver::deactivate`] if you would like the channel to remain open without keeping active
[815](https://docs.rs#815)/// receivers around.
[816](https://docs.rs#816)#[derive(Debug)]
[817](https://docs.rs#817)pub struct Receiver<T> {
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner<T>>>,
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    pos: u64,
[820](https://docs.rs#820)
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// Listens for a send or close event to unblock this stream.
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    listener: Option<EventListener>,
[823](https://docs.rs#823)}
[824](https://docs.rs#824)
[825](https://docs.rs#825)impl<T> Receiver<T> {
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    /// Returns the channel capacity.
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    ///
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    /// # Examples
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    ///
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    /// ```
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[832](https://docs.rs#832)    ///
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    /// let (_s, r) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    /// assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 5);
[835](https://docs.rs#835)    /// ```
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
[837](https://docs.rs#837)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().capacity
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    }
[839](https://docs.rs#839)
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    /// Set the channel capacity.
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    ///
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    /// There are times when you need to change the channel's capacity after creating it. If the
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    /// `new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    /// dropped to shrink the channel.
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    ///
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    /// # Examples
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    ///
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    /// ```
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    ///
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// let (s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(3);
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 3);
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    /// s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    /// s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap();
[856](https://docs.rs#856)    ///
[857](https://docs.rs#857)    /// r.set_capacity(1);
[858](https://docs.rs#858)    /// assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 1);
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
[860](https://docs.rs#860)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[862](https://docs.rs#862)    /// s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
[864](https://docs.rs#864)    ///
[865](https://docs.rs#865)    /// r.set_capacity(2);
[866](https://docs.rs#866)    /// assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 2);
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    /// s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
[868](https://docs.rs#868)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
[869](https://docs.rs#869)    /// ```
[870](https://docs.rs#870)    pub fn set_capacity(&mut self, new_cap: usize) {
[871](https://docs.rs#871)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().set_capacity(new_cap);
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    }
[873](https://docs.rs#873)
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    /// If overflow mode is enabled on this channel.
[875](https://docs.rs#875)    ///
[876](https://docs.rs#876)    /// # Examples
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    ///
[878](https://docs.rs#878)    /// ```
[879](https://docs.rs#879)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[880](https://docs.rs#880)    ///
[881](https://docs.rs#881)    /// let (_s, r) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[882](https://docs.rs#882)    /// assert!(!r.overflow());
[883](https://docs.rs#883)    /// ```
[884](https://docs.rs#884)    pub fn overflow(&self) -> bool {
[885](https://docs.rs#885)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().overflow
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    }
[887](https://docs.rs#887)
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    /// Set overflow mode on the channel.
[889](https://docs.rs#889)    ///
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    /// When overflow mode is set, broadcasting to the channel will succeed even if the channel is
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    /// full. It achieves that by removing the oldest message from the channel.
[892](https://docs.rs#892)    ///
[893](https://docs.rs#893)    /// # Examples
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    ///
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    /// ```
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    ///
[898](https://docs.rs#898)    /// let (s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    /// s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    /// s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3), Err(TrySendError::Full(3)));
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    /// r.set_overflow(true);
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap(), Some(1));
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(4).unwrap(), Some(2));
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    ///
[906](https://docs.rs#906)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
[907](https://docs.rs#907)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
[908](https://docs.rs#908)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 4);
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[910](https://docs.rs#910)    /// ```
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    pub fn set_overflow(&mut self, overflow: bool) {
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().overflow = overflow;
[913](https://docs.rs#913)    }
[914](https://docs.rs#914)
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    /// If sender will wait for active receivers.
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    ///
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    /// If set to `false`, [`Send`] will resolve immediately with a [`SendError`]. Defaults to
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    /// `true`.
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    ///
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    /// # Examples
[921](https://docs.rs#921)    ///
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    /// ```
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    ///
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    /// let (_, r) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    /// assert!(r.await_active());
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    /// ```
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    pub fn await_active(&self) -> bool {
[929](https://docs.rs#929)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().await_active
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    }
[931](https://docs.rs#931)
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    /// Specify if sender will wait for active receivers.
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    ///
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    /// If set to `false`, [`Send`] will resolve immediately with a [`SendError`]. Defaults to
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    /// `true`.
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    ///
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    /// # Examples
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    ///
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    /// ```
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    ///
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    /// let (s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    /// s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    ///
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    /// r.set_await_active(false);
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    /// let _ = r.deactivate();
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    /// assert!(s.broadcast(2).await.is_err());
[949](https://docs.rs#949)    /// # });
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    /// ```
[951](https://docs.rs#951)    pub fn set_await_active(&mut self, await_active: bool) {
[952](https://docs.rs#952)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().await_active = await_active;
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    }
[954](https://docs.rs#954)
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    /// Closes the channel.
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    ///
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    /// Returns `true` if this call has closed the channel and it was not closed already.
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    ///
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    /// The remaining messages can still be received.
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    ///
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    /// # Examples
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    ///
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    /// ```
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    ///
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    /// let (s, mut r) = broadcast(1);
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    /// assert!(s.close());
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    ///
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await.unwrap(), 1);
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    /// # });
[974](https://docs.rs#974)    /// ```
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    pub fn close(&self) -> bool {
[976](https://docs.rs#976)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().close()
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    }
[978](https://docs.rs#978)
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is closed.
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    ///
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    /// # Examples
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    ///
[983](https://docs.rs#983)    /// ```
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    ///
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<()>(1);
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    /// assert!(!s.is_closed());
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    ///
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    /// drop(r);
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    /// assert!(s.is_closed());
[992](https://docs.rs#992)    /// # });
[993](https://docs.rs#993)    /// ```
[994](https://docs.rs#994)    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().is_closed
[996](https://docs.rs#996)    }

[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)        inner.queue.len() == inner.capacity
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)    }

[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)    /// Returns the number of receivers for the channel.
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)    ///
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)    /// This does not include inactive receivers. Use [`Receiver::inactive_receiver_count`] if you
