[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)    /// Downgrade to a [`InactiveReceiver`].
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)    ///
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)    /// An inactive receiver is one that can not and does not receive any messages. Its only purpose
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)    /// is keep the associated channel open even when there are no (active) receivers. An inactive
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)    /// receiver can be upgraded into a [`Receiver`] using [`InactiveReceiver::activate`] or
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)    /// [`InactiveReceiver::activate_cloned`].
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)    ///
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)    /// [`Sender::try_broadcast`] will return [`TrySendError::Inactive`] if only inactive
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)    /// receivers exists for the associated channel and [`Sender::broadcast`] will wait until an
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)    /// active receiver is available.
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    ///
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)    /// # Examples
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)    ///
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)    /// ```
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError};
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    ///
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)    /// let inactive = r.deactivate();
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(10), Err(TrySendError::Inactive(10)));
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)    ///
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)    /// let mut r = inactive.activate();
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(10).await, Ok(None));
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Ok(10));
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)    /// # });
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    /// ```
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)    pub fn deactivate(self) -> InactiveReceiver<T> {
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)        // Drop::drop impl of Receiver will take care of `receiver_count`.
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().inactive_receiver_count += 1;
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        InactiveReceiver {
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)        }
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)    }
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)}
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)impl<T: Clone> Receiver<T> {
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)    /// Receives a message from the channel.
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)    ///
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)    /// If the channel is empty, this method waits until there is a message.
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)    ///
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)    /// If the channel is closed, this method receives a message or returns an error if there are
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)    /// no more messages.
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)    ///
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)    /// If this receiver has missed a message (only possible if overflow mode is enabled), then
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)    /// this method returns an error and readjusts its cursor to point to the first available
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)    /// message.
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)    ///
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)    /// The future returned by this function is pinned to the heap. If the future being `Unpin` is
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)    /// not important to you, or if you just `.await` this future, use the [`recv_direct`] method
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)    /// instead.
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)    ///
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)    /// # Examples
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)    ///
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)    /// ```
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)    ///
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)    /// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)    /// let mut r2 = r1.clone();
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)    ///
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)    /// drop(s);
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)    ///
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(1));
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)    /// # });
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)    /// ```
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)    pub fn recv(&mut self) -> Pin<Box<Recv<'_, T>>> {
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)        Box::pin(self.recv_direct())
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)    }
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)    /// Receives a message from the channel without pinning the future to the heap.
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)    ///
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)    /// The future returned by this method is not `Unpin` and must be pinned before use. This is
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)    /// the desired behavior if you just `.await` on the future. For other uses cases, use the
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)    /// [`recv`] method instead.
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)    ///
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)    /// # Examples
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)    ///
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)    /// ```
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)    ///
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)    /// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)    /// let mut r2 = r1.clone();
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)    ///
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)    /// drop(s);
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)    ///
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv_direct().await, Ok(1));
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv_direct().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv_direct().await, Ok(1));
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv_direct().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)    /// # });
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)    /// ```
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)    pub fn recv_direct(&mut self) -> Recv<'_, T> {
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)        Recv::_new(RecvInner {
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)            receiver: self,
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)            listener: None,
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)            _pin: PhantomPinned,
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)        })
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)    }
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)    /// Attempts to receive a message from the channel.
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)    ///
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)    /// If the channel is empty or closed, this method returns an error.
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)    ///
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)    /// If this receiver has missed a message (only possible if overflow mode is enabled), then
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)    /// this method returns an error and readjusts its cursor to point to the first available
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)    /// message.
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)    ///
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)    /// # Examples
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)    ///
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)    /// ```
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TryRecvError};
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)    ///
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)    /// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)    /// let mut r2 = r1.clone();
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)    ///
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)    /// assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Ok(1));
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)    /// assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)    /// assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Ok(1));
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)    /// assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)    ///
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)    /// drop(s);
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)    /// assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)    /// assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    /// # });
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)    /// ```
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    pub fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<T, TryRecvError> {
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)        self.inner
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)            .lock()
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)            .unwrap()
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)            .try_recv_at(&mut self.pos)
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)            .map(|cow| cow.unwrap_or_else(T::clone))
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)    }
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)    /// Receives a message from the channel using the blocking strategy.
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)    ///
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)    /// If the channel is empty, this method will block until there is a message.
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)    ///
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)    /// If the channel is closed, this method receives a message or returns an error if there are
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    /// no more messages.
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)    ///
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)    /// If this receiver has missed a message (only possible if overflow mode is enabled), then
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)    /// this method returns an error and readjusts its cursor to point to the first available
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    /// message.
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)    ///
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)    /// # Blocking
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)    ///
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)    /// Rather than using asynchronous waiting, like the [`recv`](Self::recv) method,
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    /// this method will block the current thread until the message is sent.
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    ///
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)    /// This method should not be used in an asynchronous context. It is intended
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    /// to be used such that a channel can be used in both asynchronous and synchronous contexts.
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)    /// Calling this method in an asynchronous context may result in deadlocks.
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)    ///
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    /// # Examples
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)    ///
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)    /// ```
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)    ///
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    /// let (s, mut r) = broadcast(1);
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    ///
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast_blocking(1), Ok(None));
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)    /// drop(s);
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)    ///
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv_blocking(), Ok(1));
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv_blocking(), Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    /// ```
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    #[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)    pub fn recv_blocking(&mut self) -> Result<T, RecvError> {
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)        self.recv_direct().wait()
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)    }
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)    /// Produce a new Sender for this channel.
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)    ///
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    /// This will not re-open the channel if it was closed due to all senders being dropped.
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)    ///
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)    /// # Examples
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)    ///
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    /// ```
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)    ///
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)    /// let (s1, mut r) = broadcast(2);
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)    ///
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)    /// assert_eq!(s1.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)    ///
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)    /// let mut s2 = r.new_sender();
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)    ///
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)    /// assert_eq!(s2.broadcast(2).await, Ok(None));
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)    /// drop(s1);
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)    /// drop(s2);
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)    ///
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Ok(1));
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Ok(2));
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)    /// assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    /// # });
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    /// ```
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)    pub fn new_sender(&self) -> Sender<T> {
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().sender_count += 1;
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)        Sender {
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)        }
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    }
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)    /// Produce a new Receiver for this channel.
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)    ///
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)    /// Unlike [`Receiver::clone`], this method creates a new receiver that starts with zero
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)    /// messages available.  This is slightly faster than a real clone.
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)    ///
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)    /// # Examples
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)    ///
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)    /// ```
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)    ///
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)    /// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)    ///
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)    ///
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)    /// let mut r2 = r1.new_receiver();
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)    ///
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(2).await, Ok(None));
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)    /// drop(s);
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)    ///
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(2));
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)    ///
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(2));
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)    /// # });
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)    /// ```
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)    pub fn new_receiver(&self) -> Self {
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)        inner.receiver_count += 1;
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)        Receiver {
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)            pos: inner.head_pos + inner.queue.len() as u64,
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)            listener: None,
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)        }
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)    }
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)    /// A low level poll method that is similar to [`Receiver::recv()`] or
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    /// [`Receiver::recv_direct()`], and can be useful for building stream implementations which
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)    /// use a [`Receiver`] under the hood and want to know if the stream has overflowed.
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    ///
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    /// Prefer to use [`Receiver::recv()`] or [`Receiver::recv_direct()`] when otherwise possible.
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    ///
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    /// # Errors
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    ///
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)    /// If the number of messages that have been sent has overflowed the channel capacity, a
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)    /// [`RecvError::Overflowed`] variant is returned containing the number of items that
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)    /// overflowed and were lost.
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)    ///
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)    /// # Examples
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)    ///
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)    /// This example shows how the [`Receiver::poll_recv`] method can be used to allow a custom
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)    /// stream implementation to internally make use of a [`Receiver`]. This example implementation
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)    /// differs from the stream implementation of [`Receiver`] because it returns an error if
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)    /// the channel capacity overflows, which the built in [`Receiver`] stream doesn't do.
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)    ///
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)    /// ```
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)    /// use futures_core::Stream;
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)    /// use async_broadcast::{Receiver, RecvError};
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)    /// use std::{pin::Pin, task::{Poll, Context}};
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    ///
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)    /// struct MyStream(Receiver<i32>);
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    ///
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)    /// impl futures_core::Stream for MyStream {
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)    ///     type Item = Result<i32, RecvError>;
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)    ///     fn poll_next(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Self::Item>> {
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    ///         Pin::new(&mut self.0).poll_recv(cx)
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    ///     }
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)    /// }
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    /// ```
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    pub fn poll_recv(
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)        mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)        cx: &mut Context<'_>,
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    ) -> Poll<Option<Result<T, RecvError>>> {
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)        loop {
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)            // If this stream is listening for events, first wait for a notification.
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)            if let Some(listener) = self.listener.as_mut() {
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)                ready!(Pin::new(listener).poll(cx));
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)                self.listener = None;
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)            }
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)            loop {
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)                // Attempt to receive a message.
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)                match self.try_recv() {
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)                    Ok(msg) => {
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)                        // The stream is not blocked on an event - drop the listener.
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)                        self.listener = None;
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)                        return Poll::Ready(Some(Ok(msg)));
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)                    }
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)                    Err(TryRecvError::Closed) => {
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)                        // The stream is not blocked on an event - drop the listener.
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)                        self.listener = None;
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)                        return Poll::Ready(None);
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)                    }
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)                    Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(n)) => {
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)                        // The stream is not blocked on an event - drop the listener.
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)                        self.listener = None;
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)                        return Poll::Ready(Some(Err(RecvError::Overflowed(n))));
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)                    }
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)                    Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => {}
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)                }
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)                // Receiving failed - now start listening for notifications or wait for one.
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)                match self.listener.as_mut() {
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)                    None => {
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)                        // Start listening and then try receiving again.
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)                        self.listener = {
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)                            let inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)                            Some(inner.recv_ops.listen())
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)                        };
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)                    }
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)                    Some(_) => {
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)                        // Go back to the outer loop to poll the listener.
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)                        break;
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)                    }
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)                }
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)            }
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)        }
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)    }
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)}
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)impl<T> Drop for Receiver<T> {
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)        // Remove ourself from each item's counter
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)        loop {
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)            match inner.try_recv_at(&mut self.pos) {
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)                Ok(_) => continue,
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)                Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(_)) => continue,
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)                Err(TryRecvError::Closed) => break,
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)                Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => break,
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)            }
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)        }
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)        inner.receiver_count -= 1;
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)        inner.close_channel();
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)    }
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)}
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)impl<T> Clone for Receiver<T> {
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)    /// Produce a clone of this Receiver that has the same messages queued.
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)    ///
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)    /// # Examples
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)    ///
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)    /// ```
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)    ///
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)    /// let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)    ///
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)    /// assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)    /// drop(s);
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)    ///
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)    /// let mut r2 = r1.clone();
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)    ///
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)    /// assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(1));
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)    /// assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)    /// # });
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)    /// ```
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)        inner.receiver_count += 1;
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)        // increment the waiter count on all items not yet received by this object
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)        let n = self.pos.saturating_sub(inner.head_pos) as usize;
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)        for (_elt, waiters) in inner.queue.iter_mut().skip(n) {
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)            *waiters += 1;
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)        }
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)        Receiver {
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)            pos: self.pos,
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)            listener: None,
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)        }
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)    }
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)}
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)impl<T: Clone> Stream for Receiver<T> {
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)    type Item = T;
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)    fn poll_next(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Self::Item>> {
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)        loop {
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)            match ready!(self.as_mut().poll_recv(cx)) {
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)                Some(Ok(val)) => return Poll::Ready(Some(val)),
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)                // If overflowed, we expect future operations to succeed so try again.
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)                Some(Err(RecvError::Overflowed(_))) => continue,
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)                // RecvError::Closed should never appear here, but handle it anyway.
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)                None | Some(Err(RecvError::Closed)) => return Poll::Ready(None),
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)            }
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)        }
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    }
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)}
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)impl<T: Clone> futures_core::stream::FusedStream for Receiver<T> {
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)    fn is_terminated(&self) -> bool {
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)        let inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)        inner.is_closed && inner.queue.is_empty()
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)    }
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)}

[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)/// An error returned from [`Sender::try_broadcast()`].

[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)pub enum TrySendError<T> {
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    /// The channel is full but not closed.
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)    Full(T),
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)    /// The channel is closed.
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    Closed(T),
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)    /// There are currently no active receivers, only inactive ones.

[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)}

[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    pub fn into_inner(self) -> T {
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)        match self {
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)            TrySendError::Full(t) => t,
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)            TrySendError::Closed(t) => t,
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)            TrySendError::Inactive(t) => t,
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)        }
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)    }

[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is full but not closed.
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)    pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool {
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)        match self {
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)            TrySendError::Full(_) => true,
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)            TrySendError::Closed(_) | TrySendError::Inactive(_) => false,
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)        }
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)    }
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)

[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)        match self {
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)            TrySendError::Full(_) | TrySendError::Inactive(_) => false,
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)            TrySendError::Closed(_) => true,
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)        }
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)    }
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)    /// Returns `true` if there are currently no active receivers, only inactive ones.
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)    pub fn is_disconnected(&self) -> bool {
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)        match self {
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)            TrySendError::Full(_) | TrySendError::Closed(_) => false,
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)            TrySendError::Inactive(_) => true,
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)        }
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)    }
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)}

[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)/// An error returned from [`Receiver::recv()`].
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)pub enum RecvError {
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)    /// The channel has overflowed since the last element was seen.  Future recv operations will
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)    /// succeed, but some messages have been skipped.
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)    ///
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)    /// Contains the number of messages missed.
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)    Overflowed(u64),
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)    /// The channel is empty and closed.
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)    Closed,
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)}
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)impl error::Error for RecvError {}
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)impl fmt::Display for RecvError {
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)        match self {
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)            Self::Overflowed(n) => write!(f, "receiving skipped {} messages", n),
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)            Self::Closed => write!(f, "receiving from an empty and closed channel"),
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)        }
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)    }
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)}
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)/// An error returned from [`Receiver::try_recv()`].
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)pub enum TryRecvError {
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)    /// The channel has overflowed since the last element was seen.  Future recv operations will
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)    /// succeed, but some messages have been skipped.
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)    Overflowed(u64),
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)    /// The channel is empty but not closed.
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)    Empty,
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)    /// The channel is empty and closed.
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)    Closed,
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)}
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)impl TryRecvError {
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is empty but not closed.
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)        match self {
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)            TryRecvError::Empty => true,
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)            TryRecvError::Closed => false,
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)            TryRecvError::Overflowed(_) => false,
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)        }
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)    }
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is empty and closed.
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)        match self {
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)            TryRecvError::Empty => false,
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)            TryRecvError::Closed => true,
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)            TryRecvError::Overflowed(_) => false,
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)        }
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)    }
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)    /// Returns `true` if this error indicates the receiver missed messages.
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    pub fn is_overflowed(&self) -> bool {
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)        match self {
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)            TryRecvError::Empty => false,
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)            TryRecvError::Closed => false,
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)            TryRecvError::Overflowed(_) => true,
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)        }
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)    }

[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)impl fmt::Display for TryRecvError {

[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)        match *self {
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)            TryRecvError::Empty => write!(f, "receiving from an empty channel"),
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)            TryRecvError::Closed => write!(f, "receiving from an empty and closed channel"),
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)            TryRecvError::Overflowed(n) => {

[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)            }
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)        }
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)    }

[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)    #[derive(Debug)]
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)    struct SendInner<'a, T> {
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)        sender: &'a Sender<T>,
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)        listener: Option<EventListener>,
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)        msg: Option<T>,
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)        // Keeping this type `!Unpin` enables future optimizations.
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)        #[pin]
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)        _pin: PhantomPinned
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)    }
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)}
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)impl<T: Clone> EventListenerFuture for SendInner<'_, T> {
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)    type Output = Result<Option<T>, SendError<T>>;
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)    fn poll_with_strategy<'x, S: event_listener_strategy::Strategy<'x>>(
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)        self: Pin<&mut Self>,
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)        strategy: &mut S,
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)        context: &mut S::Context,
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)    ) -> Poll<Self::Output> {
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)        let this = self.project();
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)        loop {
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)            let msg = this.msg.take().unwrap();
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)            let inner = &this.sender.inner;
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)            // Attempt to send a message.
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)            match this.sender.try_broadcast(msg) {
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)                Ok(msg) => {
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)                    let inner = inner.lock().unwrap();
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)                    if inner.queue.len() < inner.capacity {
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)                        // Not full still, so notify the next awaiting sender.
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)                        inner.send_ops.notify(1);
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)                    }
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)                    return Poll::Ready(Ok(msg));
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)                }
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)                Err(TrySendError::Closed(msg)) => return Poll::Ready(Err(SendError(msg))),
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)                Err(TrySendError::Full(m)) => *this.msg = Some(m),
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)                Err(TrySendError::Inactive(m)) if inner.lock().unwrap().await_active => {
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)                    *this.msg = Some(m)
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)                }
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)                Err(TrySendError::Inactive(m)) => return Poll::Ready(Err(SendError(m))),
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)            }
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)            // Sending failed - now start listening for notifications or wait for one.
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)            match &this.listener {
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)                None => {
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)                    // Start listening and then try sending again.
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)                    let inner = inner.lock().unwrap();
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)                    *this.listener = Some(inner.send_ops.listen());
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)                }
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)                Some(_) => {
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)                    // Wait for a notification.
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)                    ready!(strategy.poll(this.listener, context));
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)                    *this.listener = None;
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)                }
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)            }
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)        }
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)    }
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)}
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)

[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)    #[must_use = "futures do nothing unless .awaited"]
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)    pub struct Recv<'a, T: Clone>(RecvInner<'a, T> => Result<T, RecvError>);
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)    #[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]

[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)pin_project! {
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)    #[derive(Debug)]
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    struct RecvInner<'a, T> {
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)        receiver: &'a mut Receiver<T>,
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)        listener: Option<EventListener>,
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)        // Keeping this type `!Unpin` enables future optimizations.
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)        #[pin]
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)        _pin: PhantomPinned
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)    }
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)}
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)impl<T: Clone> EventListenerFuture for RecvInner<'_, T> {
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)    type Output = Result<T, RecvError>;
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)    fn poll_with_strategy<'x, S: event_listener_strategy::Strategy<'x>>(
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)        self: Pin<&mut Self>,
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)        strategy: &mut S,
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)        context: &mut S::Context,
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)    ) -> Poll<Self::Output> {
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)        let this = self.project();
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)        loop {
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)            // Attempt to receive a message.
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)            match this.receiver.try_recv() {
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)                Ok(msg) => return Poll::Ready(Ok(msg)),
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)                Err(TryRecvError::Closed) => return Poll::Ready(Err(RecvError::Closed)),
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)                Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(n)) => {
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)                    return Poll::Ready(Err(RecvError::Overflowed(n)));
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)                }
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)                Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => {}
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)            }
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)            // Receiving failed - now start listening for notifications or wait for one.
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)            match &this.listener {
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)                None => {
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)                    // Start listening and then try receiving again.
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)                    *this.listener = {
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)                        let inner = this.receiver.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)                        Some(inner.recv_ops.listen())
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)                    };
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)                }
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)                Some(_) => {
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)                    // Wait for a notification.
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)                    ready!(strategy.poll(this.listener, context));
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)                    *this.listener = None;
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)                }
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)            }
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)        }
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)    }
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)}
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)/// An inactive  receiver.
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)///
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)/// An inactive receiver is a receiver that is unable to receive messages. It's only useful for
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)/// keeping a channel open even when no associated active receivers exist.
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)#[derive(Debug)]
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)pub struct InactiveReceiver<T> {
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner<T>>>,
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)}
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)impl<T> InactiveReceiver<T> {
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)    /// Convert to an activate [`Receiver`].
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)    ///
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)    /// Consumes `self`. Use [`InactiveReceiver::activate_cloned`] if you want to keep `self`.
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)    ///
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)    /// # Examples
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)    ///
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)    /// ```
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError};
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)    ///
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)    /// let inactive = r.deactivate();
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(10), Err(TrySendError::Inactive(10)));
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)    ///
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)    /// let mut r = inactive.activate();
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(10), Ok(None));
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Ok(10));
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)    /// ```
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)    pub fn activate(self) -> Receiver<T> {
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)        self.activate_cloned()
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)    }
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)    /// Create an activate [`Receiver`] for the associated channel.
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)    ///
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)    /// # Examples
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)    ///
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)    /// ```
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)    /// use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError};
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)    ///
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)    /// let inactive = r.deactivate();
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(10), Err(TrySendError::Inactive(10)));
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)    ///
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)    /// let mut r = inactive.activate_cloned();
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)    /// assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(10), Ok(None));
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)    /// assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Ok(10));
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)    /// ```
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)    pub fn activate_cloned(&self) -> Receiver<T> {
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)        let mut inner = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)        inner.receiver_count += 1;
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)        if inner.receiver_count == 1 {
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)            // Notify 1 awaiting senders that there is now a receiver. If there is still room in the
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)            // queue, the notified operation will notify another awaiting sender.
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)            inner.send_ops.notify(1);
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)        }
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)        Receiver {
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)            inner: self.inner.clone(),
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)            pos: inner.head_pos + inner.queue.len() as u64,
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)            listener: None,
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)        }
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)    }
[1912](https://docs.rs#1912)
[1913](https://docs.rs#1913)    /// Returns the channel capacity.
[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)    ///
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)    /// See [`Receiver::capacity`] documentation for examples.
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)    pub fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().capacity
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)    }
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)    /// Set the channel capacity.
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)    ///
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)    /// There are times when you need to change the channel's capacity after creating it. If the
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)    /// `new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)    /// dropped to shrink the channel.
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)    ///
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)    /// See [`Receiver::set_capacity`] documentation for examples.
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)    pub fn set_capacity(&mut self, new_cap: usize) {
[1928](https://docs.rs#1928)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().set_capacity(new_cap);
[1929](https://docs.rs#1929)    }
[1930](https://docs.rs#1930)
[1931](https://docs.rs#1931)    /// If overflow mode is enabled on this channel.
[1932](https://docs.rs#1932)    ///
[1933](https://docs.rs#1933)    /// See [`Receiver::overflow`] documentation for examples.
[1934](https://docs.rs#1934)    pub fn overflow(&self) -> bool {
[1935](https://docs.rs#1935)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().overflow
[1936](https://docs.rs#1936)    }
[1937](https://docs.rs#1937)
[1938](https://docs.rs#1938)    /// Set overflow mode on the channel.
[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)    ///
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)    /// When overflow mode is set, broadcasting to the channel will succeed even if the channel is
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)    /// full. It achieves that by removing the oldest message from the channel.
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    ///
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    /// See [`Receiver::set_overflow`] documentation for examples.
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    pub fn set_overflow(&mut self, overflow: bool) {
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().overflow = overflow;
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    }
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    /// If sender will wait for active receivers.
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    ///
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)    /// If set to `false`, [`Send`] will resolve immediately with a [`SendError`]. Defaults to
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)    /// `true`.
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)    ///
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)    /// # Examples
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)    ///
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)    /// ```
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)    ///
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)    /// let (_, r) = broadcast::<i32>(5);
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)    /// let r = r.deactivate();
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)    /// assert!(r.await_active());
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)    /// ```
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)    pub fn await_active(&self) -> bool {
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().await_active
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)    }
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)    /// Specify if sender will wait for active receivers.
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)    ///
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)    /// If set to `false`, [`Send`] will resolve immediately with a [`SendError`]. Defaults to
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)    /// `true`.
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)    ///
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)    /// # Examples
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)    ///
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)    /// ```
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)    /// # futures_lite::future::block_on(async {
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)    /// use async_broadcast::broadcast;
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)    ///
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)    /// let (s, r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)    /// s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)    ///
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)    /// let mut r = r.deactivate();
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)    /// r.set_await_active(false);
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)    /// assert!(s.broadcast(2).await.is_err());
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)    /// # });
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)    /// ```
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)    pub fn set_await_active(&mut self, await_active: bool) {
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)        self.inner.lock().unwrap().await_active = await_active;
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)    }

[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)    /// Returns `true` if the channel is full.
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)    ///

# Sender in async_broadcast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/async-broadcast/0.7.2/async_broadcast/struct.Sender.html

`pub struct Sender<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The sending side of the broadcast channel.

Senders can be cloned and shared among threads. When all senders associated with a channel are dropped, the channel becomes closed.

The channel can also be closed manually by calling [ Sender::close()](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.close).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#353-355)#### pub fn [set_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.set_capacity)(&mut self, new_cap: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#353-355)

#### pub fn [set_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.set_capacity)(&mut self, new_cap: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Set the channel capacity.

There are times when you need to change the channel’s capacity after creating it. If the
`new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
dropped to shrink the channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
let (mut s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(3);
assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 3);
s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap();
s.set_capacity(1);
assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 1);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
s.set_capacity(2);
assert_eq!(s.capacity(), 2);
s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#394-396)#### pub fn [set_overflow](https://docs.rs#method.set_overflow)(&mut self, overflow: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#394-396)

#### pub fn [set_overflow](https://docs.rs#method.set_overflow)(&mut self, overflow: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Set overflow mode on the channel.

When overflow mode is set, broadcasting to the channel will succeed even if the channel is full. It achieves that by removing the oldest message from the channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
let (mut s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3), Err(TrySendError::Full(3)));
s.set_overflow(true);
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap(), Some(1));
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(4).unwrap(), Some(2));
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 4);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#434-436)#### pub fn [set_await_active](https://docs.rs#method.set_await_active)(&mut self, await_active: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#434-436)

#### pub fn [set_await_active](https://docs.rs#method.set_await_active)(&mut self, await_active: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Specify if sender will wait for active receivers.

If set to `false`, [ Send](https://docs.rs/struct.Send.html) will resolve immediately with a

[. Defaults to](https://docs.rs/struct.SendError.html)

`SendError``true`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::broadcast;
let (mut s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
let _ = r.deactivate();
s.set_await_active(false);
assert!(s.broadcast(2).await.is_err());
```
Closes the channel.

Returns `true` if this call has closed the channel and it was not closed already.

The remaining messages can still be received.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r) = broadcast(1);
s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
assert!(s.close());
assert_eq!(r.recv().await.unwrap(), 1);
assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
Returns the number of messages in the channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::broadcast;
let (s, r) = broadcast(2);
assert_eq!(s.len(), 0);
s.broadcast(1).await;
s.broadcast(2).await;
assert_eq!(s.len(), 2);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#631-639)#### pub fn [new_receiver](https://docs.rs#method.new_receiver)(&self) -> [Receiver](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)<T>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#631-639)

#### pub fn [new_receiver](https://docs.rs#method.new_receiver)(&self) -> [Receiver](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)<T>

Produce a new Receiver for this channel.

The new receiver starts with zero messages available. This will not re-open the channel if it was closed due to all receivers being dropped.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
let mut r2 = s.new_receiver();
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(2).await, Ok(None));
drop(s);
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(2));
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(2));
assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
Broadcasts a message on the channel.

If the channel is full, this method waits until there is space for a message unless:

- overflow mode (set through `Sender::set_overflow`
- this behavior is disabled using `Sender::set_await_active``SendError`

If the channel is closed, this method returns an error.

The future returned by this function is pinned to the heap. If the future being `Unpin` is
not important to you, or if you just `.await` this future, use the [`broadcast_direct`] method
instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, SendError};
let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
drop(r);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(2).await, Err(SendError(2)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#695-702)#### pub fn [broadcast_direct](https://docs.rs#method.broadcast_direct)(&self, msg: T) -> [Send](https://docs.rs/struct.Send.html)<'_, T> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#695-702)

#### pub fn [broadcast_direct](https://docs.rs#method.broadcast_direct)(&self, msg: T) -> [Send](https://docs.rs/struct.Send.html)<'_, T> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Broadcasts a message on the channel without pinning the future to the heap.

The future returned by this method is not `Unpin` and must be pinned before use. This is
the desired behavior if you just `.await` on the future. For other uses cases, use the
[ broadcast](https://docs.rs/fn.broadcast.html) method instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, SendError};
let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast_direct(1).await, Ok(None));
drop(r);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast_direct(2).await, Err(SendError(2)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#726-754)#### pub fn [try_broadcast](https://docs.rs#method.try_broadcast)(&self, msg: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T>, [TrySendError](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html)<T>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#726-754)

#### pub fn [try_broadcast](https://docs.rs#method.try_broadcast)(&self, msg: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T>, [TrySendError](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html)<T>>

Attempts to broadcast a message on the channel.

If the channel is full, this method returns an error unless overflow mode (set through
[ Sender::set_overflow](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.set_overflow)) is enabled. If the overflow mode is enabled, it removes the
oldest message from the channel to make room for the new message. The removed message
is returned to the caller.

If the channel is closed, this method returns an error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-17)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError};
let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(1), Ok(None));
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
drop(r);
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3), Err(TrySendError::Closed(3)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#783-785)#### pub fn [broadcast_blocking](https://docs.rs#method.broadcast_blocking)(&self, msg: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T>, [SendError](https://docs.rs/struct.SendError.html)<T>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#783-785)

#### pub fn [broadcast_blocking](https://docs.rs#method.broadcast_blocking)(&self, msg: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T>, [SendError](https://docs.rs/struct.SendError.html)<T>>

Broadcasts a message on the channel using the blocking strategy.

If the channel is full, this method will block until there is room.

If the channel is closed, this method returns an error.

[§](https://docs.rs#blocking)Blocking

Rather than using asynchronous waiting, like the [ send](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.broadcast) method,
this method will block the current thread until the message is sent.

This method should not be used in an asynchronous context. It is intended to be used such that a channel can be used in both asynchronous and synchronous contexts. Calling this method in an asynchronous context may result in deadlocks.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, SendError};
let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast_blocking(1), Ok(None));
drop(r);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast_blocking(2), Err(SendError(2)));
```

# Receiver in async_broadcast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/async-broadcast/0.7.2/async_broadcast/struct.Receiver.html

`pub struct Receiver<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The receiving side of a channel.

Receivers can be cloned and shared among threads. When all (active) receivers associated with a
channel are dropped, the channel becomes closed. You can deactivate a receiver using
[ Receiver::deactivate](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.deactivate) if you would like the channel to remain open without keeping active
receivers around.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#870-872)#### pub fn [set_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.set_capacity)(&mut self, new_cap: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#870-872)

#### pub fn [set_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.set_capacity)(&mut self, new_cap: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Set the channel capacity.

There are times when you need to change the channel’s capacity after creating it. If the
`new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
dropped to shrink the channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
let (s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(3);
assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 3);
s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap();
r.set_capacity(1);
assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 1);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
r.set_capacity(2);
assert_eq!(r.capacity(), 2);
s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(2), Err(TrySendError::Full(2)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#911-913)#### pub fn [set_overflow](https://docs.rs#method.set_overflow)(&mut self, overflow: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#911-913)

#### pub fn [set_overflow](https://docs.rs#method.set_overflow)(&mut self, overflow: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Set overflow mode on the channel.

When overflow mode is set, broadcasting to the channel will succeed even if the channel is full. It achieves that by removing the oldest message from the channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError, TryRecvError};
let (s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
s.try_broadcast(1).unwrap();
s.try_broadcast(2).unwrap();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3), Err(TrySendError::Full(3)));
r.set_overflow(true);
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(3).unwrap(), Some(1));
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(4).unwrap(), Some(2));
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Overflowed(2)));
assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 3);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv().unwrap(), 4);
assert_eq!(r.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#951-953)#### pub fn [set_await_active](https://docs.rs#method.set_await_active)(&mut self, await_active: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#951-953)

#### pub fn [set_await_active](https://docs.rs#method.set_await_active)(&mut self, await_active: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Specify if sender will wait for active receivers.

If set to `false`, [ Send](https://docs.rs/struct.Send.html) will resolve immediately with a

[. Defaults to](https://docs.rs/struct.SendError.html)

`SendError``true`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::broadcast;
let (s, mut r) = broadcast::<i32>(2);
s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
r.set_await_active(false);
let _ = r.deactivate();
assert!(s.broadcast(2).await.is_err());
```
Closes the channel.

Returns `true` if this call has closed the channel and it was not closed already.

The remaining messages can still be received.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r) = broadcast(1);
s.broadcast(1).await.unwrap();
assert!(s.close());
assert_eq!(r.recv().await.unwrap(), 1);
assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
Returns the number of messages in the channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::broadcast;
let (s, r) = broadcast(2);
assert_eq!(s.len(), 0);
s.broadcast(1).await;
s.broadcast(2).await;
assert_eq!(s.len(), 2);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1146-1153)#### pub fn [deactivate](https://docs.rs#method.deactivate)(self) -> [InactiveReceiver](https://docs.rs/struct.InactiveReceiver.html)<T>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1146-1153)

#### pub fn [deactivate](https://docs.rs#method.deactivate)(self) -> [InactiveReceiver](https://docs.rs/struct.InactiveReceiver.html)<T>

Downgrade to a [ InactiveReceiver](https://docs.rs/struct.InactiveReceiver.html).

An inactive receiver is one that can not and does not receive any messages. Its only purpose
is keep the associated channel open even when there are no (active) receivers. An inactive
receiver can be upgraded into a [ Receiver](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html) using

[or](https://docs.rs/struct.InactiveReceiver.html#method.activate)

`InactiveReceiver::activate`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.InactiveReceiver.html#method.activate_cloned)

`InactiveReceiver::activate_cloned`[ Sender::try_broadcast](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.try_broadcast) will return

[if only inactive receivers exists for the associated channel and](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html#variant.Inactive)

`TrySendError::Inactive`[will wait until an active receiver is available.](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html#method.broadcast)

`Sender::broadcast`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TrySendError};
let (s, r) = broadcast(1);
let inactive = r.deactivate();
assert_eq!(s.try_broadcast(10), Err(TrySendError::Inactive(10)));
let mut r = inactive.activate();
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(10).await, Ok(None));
assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Ok(10));
```
Receives a message from the channel.

If the channel is empty, this method waits until there is a message.

If the channel is closed, this method receives a message or returns an error if there are no more messages.

If this receiver has missed a message (only possible if overflow mode is enabled), then this method returns an error and readjusts its cursor to point to the first available message.

The future returned by this function is pinned to the heap. If the future being `Unpin` is
not important to you, or if you just `.await` this future, use the [`recv_direct`] method
instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
let mut r2 = r1.clone();
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
drop(s);
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1218-1224)#### pub fn [recv_direct](https://docs.rs#method.recv_direct)(&mut self) -> [Recv](https://docs.rs/struct.Recv.html)<'_, T> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1218-1224)

#### pub fn [recv_direct](https://docs.rs#method.recv_direct)(&mut self) -> [Recv](https://docs.rs/struct.Recv.html)<'_, T> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Receives a message from the channel without pinning the future to the heap.

The future returned by this method is not `Unpin` and must be pinned before use. This is
the desired behavior if you just `.await` on the future. For other uses cases, use the
[`recv`] method instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
let mut r2 = r1.clone();
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
drop(s);
assert_eq!(r1.recv_direct().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r1.recv_direct().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
assert_eq!(r2.recv_direct().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r2.recv_direct().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1254-1260)#### pub fn [try_recv](https://docs.rs#method.try_recv)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [TryRecvError](https://docs.rs/enum.TryRecvError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1254-1260)

#### pub fn [try_recv](https://docs.rs#method.try_recv)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [TryRecvError](https://docs.rs/enum.TryRecvError.html)>

Attempts to receive a message from the channel.

If the channel is empty or closed, this method returns an error.

If this receiver has missed a message (only possible if overflow mode is enabled), then this method returns an error and readjusts its cursor to point to the first available message.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-17)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, TryRecvError};
let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(1);
let mut r2 = r1.clone();
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Empty));
drop(s);
assert_eq!(r1.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
assert_eq!(r2.try_recv(), Err(TryRecvError::Closed));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1296-1298)#### pub fn [recv_blocking](https://docs.rs#method.recv_blocking)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [RecvError](https://docs.rs/enum.RecvError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1296-1298)

#### pub fn [recv_blocking](https://docs.rs#method.recv_blocking)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [RecvError](https://docs.rs/enum.RecvError.html)>

Receives a message from the channel using the blocking strategy.

If the channel is empty, this method will block until there is a message.

If the channel is closed, this method receives a message or returns an error if there are no more messages.

If this receiver has missed a message (only possible if overflow mode is enabled), then this method returns an error and readjusts its cursor to point to the first available message.

[§](https://docs.rs#blocking)Blocking

Rather than using asynchronous waiting, like the [ recv](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.recv) method,
this method will block the current thread until the message is sent.

This method should not be used in an asynchronous context. It is intended to be used such that a channel can be used in both asynchronous and synchronous contexts. Calling this method in an asynchronous context may result in deadlocks.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r) = broadcast(1);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast_blocking(1), Ok(None));
drop(s);
assert_eq!(r.recv_blocking(), Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r.recv_blocking(), Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1325-1331)#### pub fn [new_sender](https://docs.rs#method.new_sender)(&self) -> [Sender](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html)<T>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1325-1331)

#### pub fn [new_sender](https://docs.rs#method.new_sender)(&self) -> [Sender](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html)<T>

Produce a new Sender for this channel.

This will not re-open the channel if it was closed due to all senders being dropped.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-19)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s1, mut r) = broadcast(2);
assert_eq!(s1.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
let mut s2 = r.new_sender();
assert_eq!(s2.broadcast(2).await, Ok(None));
drop(s1);
drop(s2);
assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Ok(2));
assert_eq!(r.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1361-1369)#### pub fn [new_receiver](https://docs.rs#method.new_receiver)(&self) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1361-1369)

#### pub fn [new_receiver](https://docs.rs#method.new_receiver)(&self) -> Self

Produce a new Receiver for this channel.

Unlike [ Receiver::clone](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.clone), this method creates a new receiver that starts with zero
messages available.  This is slightly faster than a real clone.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

```
use async_broadcast::{broadcast, RecvError};
let (s, mut r1) = broadcast(2);
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(1).await, Ok(None));
let mut r2 = r1.new_receiver();
assert_eq!(s.broadcast(2).await, Ok(None));
drop(s);
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(1));
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Ok(2));
assert_eq!(r1.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Ok(2));
assert_eq!(r2.recv().await, Err(RecvError::Closed));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1404-1452)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1404-1452)

A low level poll method that is similar to [ Receiver::recv()](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.recv) or

[, and can be useful for building stream implementations which use a](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.recv_direct)

`Receiver::recv_direct()`[under the hood and want to know if the stream has overflowed.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)

`Receiver`Prefer to use [ Receiver::recv()](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.recv) or

[when otherwise possible.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.recv_direct)

`Receiver::recv_direct()`[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If the number of messages that have been sent has overflowed the channel capacity, a
[ RecvError::Overflowed](https://docs.rs/enum.RecvError.html#variant.Overflowed) variant is returned containing the number of items that
overflowed and were lost.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

This example shows how the [ Receiver::poll_recv](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.poll_recv) method can be used to allow a custom
stream implementation to internally make use of a

[. This example implementation differs from the stream implementation of](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)

`Receiver`[because it returns an error if the channel capacity overflows, which the built in](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)

`Receiver`[stream doesn’t do.](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)

`Receiver````
use futures_core::Stream;
use async_broadcast::{Receiver, RecvError};
use std::{pin::Pin, task::{Poll, Context}};
struct MyStream(Receiver<i32>);
impl futures_core::Stream for MyStream {
    type Item = Result<i32, RecvError>;
    fn poll_next(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Self::Item>> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.0).poll_recv(cx)
    }
}
```

# InactiveReceiver in async_broadcast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/async-broadcast/0.7.2/async_broadcast/struct.InactiveReceiver.html

`pub struct InactiveReceiver<T> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An inactive receiver.

An inactive receiver is a receiver that is unable to receive messages. It’s only useful for keeping a channel open even when no associated active receivers exist.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1927-1929)#### pub fn [set_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.set_capacity)(&mut self, new_cap: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

#### pub fn [set_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.set_capacity)(&mut self, new_cap: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Set the channel capacity.

There are times when you need to change the channel’s capacity after creating it. If the
`new_cap` is less than the number of messages in the channel, the oldest messages will be
dropped to shrink the channel.

See [ Receiver::set_capacity](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.set_capacity) documentation for examples.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1944-1946)#### pub fn [set_overflow](https://docs.rs#method.set_overflow)(&mut self, overflow: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/async_broadcast/lib.rs.html#1944-1946)

#### pub fn [set_overflow](https://docs.rs#method.set_overflow)(&mut self, overflow: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Set overflow mode on the channel.

When overflow mode is set, broadcasting to the channel will succeed even if the channel is full. It achieves that by removing the oldest message from the channel.

See [ Receiver::set_overflow](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html#method.set_overflow) documentation for examples.
